Mira Patel: Quick sync: we promised concrete answers after the continuous-batcher RFC. Two open items: (1) queue decomposition strategy for utilization vs isolation, (2) kernel-selection timing and its impact on scheduling. Let's capture a deployable plan.
Daniel Cho: Short version: prefer shared-lanes for better GPU utilization, but preserve isolation via a soft-credit system and fast eviction hooks. We need clear invariants for when credit borrowing is allowed.
Esha Iyer: In sims shared-lanes increased utilization by ~12% but p99 drifted for noisy tenants. Soft credits helped but we saw oscillation under certain burst patterns. We should add a borrow_rate cap and a damping mechanism.
Rajesh Nair: On kernels: if we delay kernel decision until batch-formation finishes, we can pick shape-optimal kernels. But that ties scheduling to kernel readiness and introduces first-batch latency. Pre-binding kernels at admission gives predictability.
Jon Wells: We can do a hybrid: maintain a small set of precompiled kernel shapes (common seq-len x batch combos) and treat anything else as "dynamic" that pays a small compile penalty. Scheduler marks batches as precompiled vs dynamic upfront (fast-path vs slow-path).
Mira Patel: Proposal: roll out shared-lanes + soft-credit ledger + hybrid kernel set. Canary mode: dynamic kernels off by default; enable per-tenant opt-in. Metrics gates control rollout.
Daniel Cho: Implementation notes: credit ledger = per-tenant integer tokens, replenished on a decay schedule. Borrowing increases debt; debt amortization happens when system idle. Add metric: tenant_credit_utilization and tenant_credit_debt.
Esha Iyer: Oscillation detection: compute borrow_rate = borrowed_tokens / total_tokens over sliding 2m window. If > 15% sustained, trigger coalesce_damping: reduce max_coalesce_ms from 10->4 on host and attach 45s cooldown.
Rajesh Nair: For kernel pipeline: precompiled_set = {seq64_batch8, seq128_batch4, seq256_batch2} (start small). Admission checks shape fingerprint against set. If miss, mark batch dynamic and route to runtime-selector pool. Track kernel_miss_rate.
Jon Wells: Telemetry flags we'll use: cb.decomposition=shared_lanes, cb.kernel_mode=hybrid, cb.borrow_threshold=0.15. Also add an ops endpoint /ops/cb-drain-tenant to force immediate demotion to micro-queue for a tenant.
infra-bot: Canary cluster requested: cb-hybrid-canary. Feature flag: cb.v3.enable=true. Deploy ticket: https://go/redwood/deploys/CB-HYBRID-CANARY-3777
Mira Patel: Runbook intent: start 1% traffic to canary, increase to 5% if p99 and fairness within thresholds. Primary thresholds: p99 <= baseline * 1.2, throughput skew median dev <= 12%. Rollback if p99 > baseline*1.3 for 10m.
Daniel Cho: Add automated guard: if tenant_credit_debt_pct > 40% for 3 consecutive windows, reduce that tenant's borrow allowance and emit alert.
Esha Iyer: Tests: (a) unit tests for ledger invariants (no negative tokens, eventual restitution), (b) integration with chaos: spawn noisy tenant at 70% sustained and assert damping triggers.
Rajesh Nair: Perf microbench: measure first-batch compile latency for dynamic shapes. If compile > 150ms often, we should precompile next-hot shapes automatically.
Jon Wells: Dashboards: create cb-hybrid-canary board with p50/p95/p99, borrow_rate, credit_debt_pct, kernel_miss_rate, first_batch_compile_ms. Link alerts for guard thresholds.
Mira Patel: Owners and ETA: Daniel - credit ledger + borrow metric (3d). Esha - oscillation detector + damping (4d). Rajesh - precompiled_set + auto-compile-hotter-shapes probe (5d). Jon - flags + dashboards + canary cluster (1d). Priya (cc): can you write the short runbook?
infra-bot: Canary cluster cb-hybrid-canary scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC.
Mira Patel: One more decision: eviction behavior. We prefer graduated response: damp -> throttle bursts -> demote traffic -> emergency micro-queue eviction only if canary SLO breached repeatedly. No hard kills early.
Daniel Cho: Agree. Also add a safe-mode host flag to force precompiled-only for load tests.
Esha Iyer: And capture a postmortem template to record any fairness regressions during experiment.
Rajesh Nair: Final note: make the kernel_miss_rate a primary signal for whether to expand precompiled_set. If miss_rate > 5% for 1h, autosuggest new compile targets.
Jon Wells: I'll wire alerts: miss_rate > 5% sustained 1h => pager, borrow_rate > 0.15 sustained 2m => paging on-call for investigation.
Mira Patel: Okay if I merge this into the RFC follow-up doc and tag everyone? :thumbsup:
Daniel Cho: ack
Esha Iyer: ack
Rajesh Nair: ack
Jon Wells: ack
